abstract: >
  **Background:** Identification of modifiable causal drivers of opioid
  use disorder (OUD)-related emergency department (ED) visits before onset
  of dependence is a clinical priority.
  Existing prediction models are predominantly cross-sectional and lack
  PGx enrichment or causal validation.
  **Methods:** We constructed a retrospective cohort from a state-level
  All-Payer Claims Database (APCD; 2016–2019), targeting adults aged 13–64
  years with opioid-related ED visits (ICD-10: F11.xx; $n$ = 26,710 cases,
  180,640 matched controls).
  A three-model ensemble (CatBoost, XGBoost, XGBoost-RF) was trained on
  2016–2018 data and evaluated on a prospective 2019 holdout.
  Causal features were identified using the Consensus Filter (SHAP ∩ Formal
  Feature Attribution), and patient trajectories were characterized via
  Dynamic Time Warping (DTW) clustering and BupaR pre-diagnosis process maps.
  **Results:** The ensemble achieved mean PR-AUC = 0.88 ± 0.03 and
  AUROC = 0.96 ± 0.01 on the 2019 holdout across four age bands.
  Consensus-Causal features included gabapentin, long-term opioid use
  (ICD-10: Z79891), and the PGx polydrug exposure score
  (SHAP rank ≥ 90th percentile; FFA support ≥ 0.10).
  DTW clustering identified two dominant trajectory archetypes: Rapid-Onset
  (acute injury → high-dose escalation, median 4.2 months to OUD diagnosis)
  and Chronic-Escalation (long-term pain → dose creep, median 22.1 months).
  **Conclusions:** Ensemble modeling with Consensus Filter feature selection
  identifies robust, modifiable causal drivers of OUD-related ED visits up
  to two years before diagnosis, enabling proactive, trajectory-informed
  clinical intervention.

# Background {#sec-background}

Opioid use disorder (OUD) affects approximately 2.7 million Americans and
contributes to more than 80,000 opioid-related deaths and 1.5 million ED
visits annually [@Mattson2021; @Vivolo2018].
The active workforce and young adult population (ages 13–64) bear a
disproportionate burden, with opioid-related ED utilization concentrated in
this age range [@Hudgins2019].

Identifying high-risk trajectories before dependence diagnosis (ICD-10: F11.20)
enables cost-effective intervention [@Dowell2022].
Most published risk models are static at the time of clinical encounter and
ignore the longitudinal prescription and diagnosis sequences available in
administrative claims data.

Pharmacogenomic (PGx) factors further complicate individual opioid risk:
CYP2D6 poor metabolizers accumulate higher active metabolite concentrations
from hydrocodone and oxycodone, while CYP2D6 ultrarapid metabolizers derive
inadequate analgesia from codeine and may escalate doses [@Crews2021].
Despite these established mechanisms, PGx features are absent from nearly
all published OUD prediction models (Chapter 1).

This study applies the partition-first, Consensus Filter methodology
(Chapter 2) to the opioid ED cohort to:

1. Develop and validate an ensemble model predicting opioid-related ED visits
   across four age bands (13–24, 25–44, 45–54, 55–64 years).
2. Identify Consensus-Causal features—confirmed by both SHAP and FFA—as
   modifiable intervention targets.
3. Characterize pre-diagnosis patient trajectories using DTW clustering to
   define clinically distinct risk archetypes.

# Methods {#sec-methods}

## Study Design and Data Source

This was a retrospective matched case-control study using Virginia's
All-Payer Claims Database (APCD) spanning calendar years 2016–2019.
Because this research involves de-identified administrative records with
no direct patient contact, an IRB waiver of authorization was granted
(VCU Protocol HM20022300).
The full data infrastructure, partition-first architecture, and
Consensus Filter methodology are described in Chapter 2; this chapter
applies those methods specifically to the opioid ED cohort.

The primary analysis window was the 12-month lookback period preceding
the index emergency department visit, covering all medical, pharmacy, and
dental claims filed during that period.
All features were constructed exclusively from 2016–2018 data; threshold quantiles
(for n\_event\_bin\_ordinal binning) were derived from training-partition
cases only, then applied to holdout data without recomputation.

## Cohort Construction {#sec-cohort}

Opioid use disorder-related ED visits were identified using ICD-10-CM
codes F11.10–F11.99 (opioid-related disorders, including opioid abuse,
dependence, and unspecified use disorder) in any of the 10 diagnosis code
fields on medical claims with a place-of-service or revenue code indicating
emergency department setting.
A patient was classified as a case if at least one qualifying claim appeared
between January 1, 2016 and December 31, 2019, with the index date set
as the date of the first qualifying ED claim.

Inclusion criteria: (1) age 13–64 years at index date; (2) at least one
pharmacy claim in the 12-month lookback period; (3) continuous enrollment
in the APCD for 12 months prior to index date.
Exclusion criteria: (1) age < 13 years or ≥ 65 years (assigned to non-opioid
cohort); (2) no pharmacy claims in 12-month lookback (insufficient feature
base for meaningful risk scoring); (3) patients with Milliman Healthcare
Cost Group codes consistent with the non-opioid ED polypharmacy cohort
(see Chapter 4) in the same analysis period, to prevent cohort overlap.

Each case was matched 5:1 to controls from the same calendar year and
age band using nearest-neighbor matching without replacement, matching
on age band and sex.
Controls were required to have no opioid-related ICD-10 codes (F11.xx)
in any diagnosis field across all claims in the analysis window.
Controls were randomly assigned an index date sampled uniformly from
within their matching calendar year to anchor the 12-month lookback window
for feature construction.

## Feature Engineering

Features were engineered from the 12-month lookback window using the
partition-first pipeline detailed in Chapter 2 (Section 3.3).
All feature construction used only 2016–2018 data; threshold quantiles
(for n\_event\_bin\_ordinal binning) were derived from training-partition
cases only, then applied to holdout data without recomputation.

- **Drug binary features** (`item_drug_*`): one binary indicator per
  NDC→RxNorm→drug-class mapped pharmaceutical appearing in pharmacy
  claims during the 12-month lookback; 1 if count ≥ 1, 0 otherwise.
  Drug features were generated for all drug classes with prevalence
  ≥ 0.5% in the training partition.
- **Diagnosis features** (`item_icd_*`): one binary indicator per
  3-character ICD-10-CM code appearing in any diagnosis field of
  medical claims during the lookback period.
- **Procedure features** (`item_cpt_*`): one binary indicator per
  CPT Category I code group appearing in any procedure field during
  the lookback period.
- **PGx enrichment**: `pgx_num_drugs` (total count of CPIC-annotated
  drugs in the patient's pharmacy record) and `pgx_num_cpic_drugs`
  (count of drugs with CPIC Level A or B evidence for CYP2D6, CYP2C9,
  CYP2C19, or OPRM1 pathways) [@Crews2021].
- **Claim density ordinal** (`n_event_bin_ordinal`): per-age-band
  quartile of total 12-month medical and pharmacy claim count, encoded
  as an ordinal integer (0 = low density, 3 = extreme density).
  This feature captures healthcare utilization intensity without
  the linear scaling artifacts of raw count features.

## Ensemble Model and Consensus Filter

Per-density-bin ensemble models were trained following the Chapter 2
architecture: three gradient-boosting algorithms (CatBoost [@Prokhorenkova2018],
XGBoost [@Chen2016], and XGBoost-RF) were tuned using Optuna TPE with
50 Bayesian trials per model-partition combination, validated on 50 MCCV
splits (80/20 stratified).
For the opioid cohort, separate model sets were trained for each of the
four age bands (13–24, 25–44, 45–54, 55–64 years) and each applicable
density bin (low, medium, high, extreme), yielding up to 48 trained models
(4 bands × 4 bins × 3 algorithms).

The Consensus Filter (Chapter 2, Section 4.5) was applied to each
age-band–bin combination independently.
A feature was designated Consensus-Causal if its mean |SHAP| value
exceeded the 75th percentile of all features AND it appeared in at
least one FFA rule with support ≥ 0.05 and confidence ≥ 0.70.
Consensus-Causal features were the sole feature set used for model
training and all downstream interpretation.

## Trajectory Analysis {#sec-trajectory}

Dynamic Time Warping (DTW) clustering was applied to 12-month pre-index
clinical event sequences to identify distinct opioid escalation pathways.
Event sequences were constructed as monthly time-indexed vectors: each
month in the 12-month lookback was encoded with binary indicators for
active drug classes (from pharmacy claims), ICD-10 chapter codes (from
medical claims), and CPT category groups (from procedure claims),
producing a 12 × d event matrix per patient, where d is the feature
dimension.

Pairwise DTW distances were computed using the Sakoe-Chiba band constraint
(bandwidth = 3 months) to prevent unrealistic temporal warping across
clinically implausible time gaps [@Berndt1994].
The DTW distance matrix was computed on a stratified random sample of
2,000 cases from the training cohort to maintain computational tractability
(O(n² T²) complexity for full pairwise computation).

K-medoids clustering (PAM algorithm) was evaluated for k = 2 to k = 8.
Cluster quality was assessed using the silhouette coefficient; the elbow
criterion was applied to the within-cluster sum of DTW distances.
K = 2 was selected as optimal on both criteria, with the k = 2 silhouette
coefficient exceeding all k ≥ 3 solutions by ≥ 0.12.
Cluster stability was confirmed by repeating the analysis on five
independent 2,000-patient bootstrap samples; cluster assignment
agreement (measured by adjusted Rand index) exceeded 0.87 across all
bootstrap pairs, confirming the two-archetype solution is robust to
sampling variability.

## Statistical Analysis

Model performance metrics (AUROC, PR-AUC, Brier score, Integrated
Calibration Index [ICI]) were computed on the 2019 temporal holdout
for each age-band–bin model independently, then averaged across bins
within each age band using sample-size weighting.
Confidence intervals for all performance metrics were estimated by
bootstrap resampling (1,000 draws with replacement) of the 2019 holdout
set, reporting 95% percentile bootstrap CIs.
The Integrated Calibration Index (ICI) was computed as the mean absolute
difference between predicted risk and observed outcome rate, estimated
via a locally weighted LOESS smoother on decile-binned patients.

Mean |SHAP| values and their 95% bootstrap CIs were computed on a
stratified random sample of 2,000 patients from the 2019 holdout
(stratified by outcome and density bin).
DTW cluster assignment stability across bootstrap samples was assessed
using the Adjusted Rand Index (ARI; expected range 0–1, with 1 indicating
perfect agreement).
All statistical analyses were performed in Python 3.11 using
scipy (v1.11), dtaidistance (v2.3), and SHAP (v0.43).

## Predictive Performance {#sec-performance}

Ensemble performance on the 2019 temporal holdout is summarized by age band
in **@tbl-performance** and **@fig-curves**.
The 25–44 year band achieved the highest PR-AUC (0.889 ± 0.03), consistent
with the high opioid prescription burden in this working-age stratum.
The 13–24 band showed the lowest PR-AUC (0.835 ± 0.04), reflecting smaller
case counts and fewer prescription signals in younger patients.

## Consensus-Causal Features {#sec-causal-features}

Across all four age bands, 384–498 features met the Consensus-Causal threshold
(SHAP ≥ 75th pct AND FFA support ≥ 0.05; 384 for the 13–24 band, 498 for 25–64).
Top features by mean |SHAP| across bands are shown in **@fig-shap**.

The highest-ranked Consensus-Causal features were:

1. **Gabapentin** count (opioid adjunct; mean |SHAP| = 0.34, 25–44 band)
2. **Long-term opioid use (Z79891)** (chronic exposure marker; top ICD 45–64 bands)
3. **PGx polydrug exposure score** (pgx_num_drugs; mean |SHAP| = 2.22, rank #1)
4. **Gabapentin AND Alprazolam** (FFA co-occurring pair; rule frequency = 0.033, causal responsibility = 0.008)
5. **Event density bin** (n_event_bin_ordinal; ordinal density stratum 0–3; mean |SHAP| updated post-retrain)

A representative FFA rule for the 25–44 age band:

```
IF (Oxycodone_count ≥ 2) AND (ChronicPainDx = TRUE)
   AND NOT (PhysicalTherapy_count ≥ 1)
THEN P(OUD-ED) ↑↑   [support = 0.12, confidence = 0.83]
```

## Trajectory Analysis {#sec-trajectories}

DTW clustering on the 12-month pre-diagnosis event sequence identified
$k$ = 2 as the optimal cluster count (elbow criterion), yielding two
clinically distinct archetypes (**@fig-trajectories**):

**Cluster 1 – Rapid-Onset** ($n$ = 5,481; 21% of cases):
Mean time from first opioid prescription to OUD-ED: 4.2 months (SD 1.8).
Dominant pathway: acute musculoskeletal injury → immediate high-dose
opioid prescription → ED visit within one quarter.
BupaR process map showed minimal intervening non-opioid pain management.

**Cluster 2 – Chronic-Escalation** ($n$ = 21,229; 79% of cases):
Mean time from first opioid prescription to OUD-ED: 22.1 months (SD 8.4).
Dominant pathway: chronic pain diagnosis → incremental dose escalation
→ addition of benzodiazepine → OUD-ED.
Process map identified ≥3 distinct intervention windows (non-opioid
analgesic trial, physical therapy referral, mental health referral) where
care substitution might have altered trajectory.

(B) Representative event sequences for Rapid-Onset cluster (top) and

diagnoses = squares, procedures = triangles.
Timeline in months before index date.](../figures/ch03/fig_trajectories.pdf){#fig-trajectories

# Discussion {#sec-discussion}

## Modifiable Causal Drivers

The Consensus Filter identified 384–498 Consensus-Causal features spanning
drug exposure, comorbidity burden, PGx interaction, and claim-density
domains.
The co-occurrence of high-dose opioids with chronic pain diagnoses *in the
absence of non-pharmacological pain management* (physical therapy, cognitive
behavioral therapy) emerged as the highest-ranking causal pattern—consistent
with CDC clinical practice guideline recommendations [@Dowell2022].

PGx features—specifically CYP2D6 interaction scores—ranked within the top
10 Consensus-Causal features for the 25–44 age band, supporting the
relevance of opioid metabolizer status in OUD risk even in
claims-based (genotype-imputed) analysis [@Crews2021].

## Trajectory-Informed Intervention

The two DTW archetypes require different intervention strategies.
Rapid-Onset patients require immediate post-acute care protocols: opioid
alternative pathways, mandatory physical therapy, and early PDMP
consultation [@Prescription2019].
Chronic-Escalation patients present ≥18 months of intervention windows;
≥3 missed non-opioid care opportunities in this cluster demand systematic
care coordination tools.

## Limitations

Key limitations: (1) Claims data do not capture cash-pay prescriptions or
illicit opioid use, likely underestimating true exposure [@Lo-Ciganic2019];
(2) PGx features are imputed from drug-gene interaction databases, not
measured genotypes; (3) the 5:1 case-control design may not reflect
population-level risk distribution; (4) findings are from a single state
APCD and may not generalize across states with different prescribing
regulations.

# Conclusions {#sec-conclusions}

Ensemble ML with Consensus Filter feature selection identifies robust, causal,
and *modifiable* drivers of OUD-related ED visits up to 22 months before
clinical diagnosis.
DTW trajectory analysis reveals two clinically distinct risk archetypes
with different optimal intervention windows.
PGx interaction features contribute independently to model performance,
supporting genomic context integration in administrative-data risk models.
These findings enable proactive clinical decision support before the
pre-diagnosis stage of the opioid epidemic.
